newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT says cable news due "soon".
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT says cable news due "soon".

text.p: Post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV (Dutch PTT) said on Tuesday complex talks about the future management of its 76 percent owned cable TV firm Casema were continuing and an announcement could be expected soon.

The company on Monday announced it was breaking off talks with Philips Communications over combining their cable TV interests, which might have created a European firm with some 3.5 million cable connections.
"We've discussions with other parties and don't want to say the exact reasons we finished the talks (with Philips)," said a Dutch PTT spokesman. "We can expect an announcement soon."

Dutch PTT had been seeking to dilute its stake in Casema, which has connections to 1.2 million Dutch homes, to meet government requirements that it cut its management influence over Casema as cable telephony competition widens out.
"It's a pity for Dutch PTT," said Steven Vrolijk, analyst at ING Barings. "A combination with Philips would have provided them with a solution for the Casema issue."

Analysts said Dutch PTT might have limited options to forge another one-stop partnership as European telephony regulators would home in on any future combinations of major EU players, while U.S. operators would have other options.

"I can't see the EU allowing a player like, for instance Deutsche Telekom, to get involved in a cable firm with Dutch PTT and then watch them compete with new operators," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
Others suggested Dutch PTT might hive off parts of the Casema network to the regional energy and cable TV companies, who have laid down their markers to compete in telephony.
"There aren't really any other big potential alliance partners left in the Netherlands," said another analyst. "The regional networks might be interested but they're a bit fragmented," he added.

Another option is for Dutch PTT to hold Casema at arm's length by allowing it to become what is known as a Structuur Vennootschap, a Dutch mechanism which would insulate the unit from the influence of its parent's directors.
Analysts said a stock flotation for part of Casema might now be another solution for diluting its holding if another partnership prospect cannot be found.
"In my opinion a listing could be easier to get than another partner," said Vrolijk, "but you never know."
Philips has combined with United International Holdings in a 50:50 joint venture called UPC to exploit cable opportunities.

A Philips spokesman declined to comment on the end of the talks with Dutch PTT. He said the venture would continue acquiring new systems when opportunities presented themselves and continue to invest in laying down new networks. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
